'''Marcus E. Raichle''' (born March 15, 1937) is an American neurologist at the [[Washington University School of Medicine]] in [[St. Louis]]. He is a professor in the Department of Radiology with joint appointments in Neurology, Neurobiology and Biomedical Engineering.  His research over the past 40 years has focused on the nature of functional [[Neuroimaging|brain imaging signals]] arising from [[Positron emission tomography|PET]] and [[Functional magnetic resonance imaging|fMRI]] and the application of these techniques to the study of the human [[brain]] in health and disease.<ref name = AcadSci /> He received the [[Kavli Prize]] in Neuroscience "for the discovery of specialized brain networks for memory and cognition", together with [[Brenda Milner]] and [[John O'Keefe (neuroscientist)|John O'Keefe]] in 2014.

==Career==
Noteworthy accomplishments of Marcus Raichle include the discovery of the relative independence of blood flow and oxygen consumption during changes in brain activity which provided the physiological basis of fMRI;<ref name=Petersen>{{cite journal|last=Petersen|first=SE|author2=Fox PT |author3=Posner MI |author4=Mintun M |author5=Raichle ME |title=Positron emission tomographic studies of the cortical anatomy of single-word processing|journal=Nature|year=1988|volume=331|pages=585–589|pmid=3277066|doi=10.1038/331585a0|issue=6157|bibcode=1988Natur.331..585P |s2cid=4369305}}</ref> the discovery of a [[default mode network]] of brain function (i.e., organized intrinsic activity) and its signature system,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Raichle|first1=M. E.|last2=MacLeod|first2=A. M.|last3=Snyder|first3=A. Z.|last4=Powers|first4=W. J.|last5=Gusnard|first5=D. A.|last6=Shulman|first6=G. L.|date=January 16, 2001|title=A default mode of brain function|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|volume=98|issue=2|pages=676–682|doi=10.1073/pnas.98.2.676|issn=0027-8424|pmid=11209064|pmc=14647|doi-access=free}}</ref> the brain's [[Default network|default mode network]];<ref name=Fox>{{cite journal|last=Fox|first=MD|author2=Zhang D |author3=Snyder DZ |author4=Raichle ME |title=The global signal and observed anticorrelated resting state brain networks|journal=J. Neurophysiol.|year=2009|volume=101|pages=3270–3283|pmid=19339462|doi=10.1152/jn.90777.2008|issue=6|pmc=2694109}}</ref> and, the discovery that [[aerobic glycolysis]] contributes to brain function independent of [[oxidative phosphorylation]].<ref name=Vaishnavi>{{cite journal|last=Vaishnavi|first=SN|author2=Vlassenko AG |author3=Rundle MM |author4=Snyder AZ |author5=Mintun MA |author6=Raichle ME |title=Regional aerobic glycolysis in the human brain|journal=PNAS|year=2010|volume=107|pages=17757–17762|pmid=20837536|doi=10.1073/pnas.1010459107|issue=41|pmc=2955101|bibcode=2010PNAS..10717757V |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=Vlassenko>{{cite journal |vauthors=Vlassenko AG, Vaishnavi SN, Couture L, Sacco D, Shannon BJ, Mac, RH, Morris JC, Raichle ME, Mintun MA |title=Spatial correlation between brain aerobic glycolysis and amyloid-β deposition|journal=PNAS|year=2010|volume=107|pages=17763–17767|pmid=20837517|doi=10.1073/pnas.1010461107|issue=41|pmc=2955133|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Honors==
* Member: [[National Academy of Sciences]], [[National Academy of Medicine]], [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]
*Foreign member: [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters|The Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dnva.no/medlemmer/53|title=Utenlandske medlemmer {{!}} Det Norske Videnskaps-Akademi|website=www.dnva.no|access-date=January 28, 2020}}</ref>
* Fellow: [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]

==Awards==
In 2001, he was a co-recipient of a [[Grawemeyer Awards|Grawemeyer Award]] in Psychology, with Michael Posner and Steven Petersen of the [[University of Louisville]].<ref name=grawemeyer.org>{{cite web|title=2001– Michael Posner, Marcus Raichle and Steven Petersen|url=http://grawemeyer.org/psychology/previous-winners/2001-michael-posner-marcus-raichle-and-steven-petersen.html|work=grawemeyer.org|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521215451/http://grawemeyer.org/psychology/previous-winners/2001-michael-posner-marcus-raichle-and-steven-petersen.html|archive-date=May 21, 2014}}</ref> In 2010, he was awarded the [[Metlife Foundation Award for Medical Research in Alzheimer's Disease]] along with [[Randy Buckner]],<ref name=MetLife>{{Cite web|url=http://mlfawards.afar.org/docs/2016Edition_MetLifeFoundationAwards_PastWinners.pdf|title=MetLife Foundation Awards for Medical Research in Alzheimer's Disease|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181013093256/http://mlfawards.afar.org/docs/2016Edition_MetLifeFoundationAwards_PastWinners.pdf|archive-date=October 13, 2018}}</ref> and the [[Ariëns Kappers Medal]] from the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. In 2014, he was a co-recipient of the [[Kavli Prize]] in Neuroscience, awarded by the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]], with [[Brenda Milner]] of the [[Montreal Neurological Institute]] at [[McGill University]] and John O'Keefe of [[University College London]].<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Nine Scientists Share Three Kavli Prizes|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/nine-scientists-share-three-kavli-prizes|author=Bhattacharjee, Yudhijit |date=May 29, 2014}}</ref>
